decision.title: A streamed writer for the html and xhtml methods (packet stream-2)

item.p: Decided: the streamed serialization (src/serialize_xml.c, glossary ) takes the html method without indent and the xhtml method on the xml method's conditions (no indent, canonical, doctype-system, doctype-public or standalone); sxml_serialization_streams says so. The principal stream () resolves XSLT's indent default (yes for html and xhtml, XSLT 4.0, 26.1.4) before it asks, as the tree path does. The xml method's machinery is reused, no second writer: each element is written from a window of its own by sxml_xml_writer_open_element, so void elements, raw text (script, style), boolean and URI attributes, html-version 5 or 4.01 and the HTML processing instructions are the element's own.

Bounded state for what needs context: the document type declaration is written before the first element from the top level so far (non-whitespace text before it means no <!DOCTYPE html>, Serialization 4.0, 6.1.11, 7.5.8); include-content-type writes the meta element with head's start tag (an empty head is closed at once) and skips a meta element it replaces with its content by a depth count (6.1.18, 7.5.14); prefix normalization's "an attribute of the element or an ancestor uses the prefix" also looks at the open windows (the writer's ancestor_windows, NULL for a whole tree); the XHTML, SVG and MathML namespaces are looked up again when an element names a namespace, since the evaluation may intern one after the writer starts; top-level text is written as text, CDATA requests ignored, as sequence normalization joins it (this also aligns the xml method's streamed output with its tree). normalization-form needs no fallback: text events are joined into a text node before they are written, as for xml ().

Falls back to the tree, and why: indent=yes, for every method: whether an element is indented depends on all its children (a non-whitespace text child or an inline element child anywhere makes it not indented, 5.1.4, 6.1.5, 7.5.3), and that decides the whitespace before its first child; the deciding child can be the last event of the document, so bounded memory cannot give the same bytes (buffering the undecided output would hold the whole body). Rejected: changing the indentation rule (outputs would change). XHTML with a document type declaration or standalone (SEPM0004 reads the whole tree) and canonical. So xsl:output method="html" without indent="no" still builds the tree (now linear, ).

Measured (release CLI, peak resident set, 20,000 records of 1 KB, a streamable mode): html indent=no with a p element a record 29.8 -> 10.9 MB, with one long text node under body 59.1 -> 10.9 MB; xhtml indent=no 29.3 -> 10.9 MB; xml 10.9 MB; html with the default indent 29.8 and 59.2 MB (the tree, unchanged); every output byte-identical before and after.

Verified: serialize_html streamed_matches_tree (7 documents x 10 parameter sets; text events split into one event per character, so borders fall inside script and around multi-byte characters) and streamed_allocation_failures; evaluator_stream html_principal_result_streams (html, html by evidence with 4.01, xhtml; 30,000 records under a 1 MB limit, peaks 207 to 384 KB; byte readers of 1,000 and 3 bytes; equal to serializing the TREE delivery). XT40 whole catalog, release driver, case by case: 12,185 passed and 98 wrong error before and after, no outcome differs. QT4 XQ40 method-html, method-xhtml, method-xml, fn-serialize, method-adaptive as in CONFORMANCE.md. No public header changes (). sxml.wasm not rebuilt (about 250 lines of internal C, no new tables).
